notes: Summary: Trellis Latency Works is an enterprise payments platform evaluating Redwood Dedicated for real-time chat and transaction classification. Primary ask: a predictable reserved-GPU plan that guarantees sustained throughput during peak trading windows and sub-200ms 95th percentile latency for chat use. Baseline metrics (customer-provided): steady-state 400 QPS (avg 12 tokens/resp), peak bursts to 1,800 QPS for 7-12 minute windows during settlement spikes; average response tokens 35; estimated token/sec steady-state ~16800 tok/sec, peak burst ~126k tok/sec. Workshop outcomes: - Measured baseline with replayed traces — average token/sec per H100 instance with q4 quant = ~18k tok/sec with batching 8; A100 numbers roughly 12-14k tok/sec. - Recommendation: reserve 6 x H100-equivalents for steady-state (accounts for 6 x 18k = 108k tok/sec) plus 2x burst-capacity GPUs behind autoscaling/burst pool to hit 126k+ peak with headroom. - Latency SLO discussion: customer requires 95p <= 120-200ms depending on model complexity. Proposed plan: profile with continuous batching window 40ms, KV prefix cache for frequent prompts, and per-route SLO mapping (gold/silver routes). - SLA asks: throughput guarantees during defined settlement windows (customer wants contractual commitment for QPS floor + credit policy for missed targets). Legal is pushing to limit credits; we will propose a tiered credit model tied to percent downtime and missed throughput windows. - Security: VPC + KMS + audit logs required; data residency to remain in us-east-1. - POC: 2-week realistic traffic replay, measure 50th/95th/99th pct latency and token/sec, validate fallback to smaller quantized model if capacity constrained. Quotes/notes from stakeholders: "We can tolerate occasional slight degradation, but not during settlement spikes — that has direct revenue impact." Next steps: finalize sizing workbook (Priya to update with measured kernels and kernel-ids), legal to confirm residency clause, finance to approve reserved capacity commit. Open items: exact model selection (customer prefers open LLMs; engineering pushed Redwood-optimized variants), clarify billing for burst GPUs, confirm canary rollback plan for model rollouts.
use_case_summary: Trellis uses LLM for low-latency chat support and automated transaction classification at settlement. Needs deterministic capacity for peak windows, per-route latency SLOs, and private VPC with KMS. Looking at Dedicated with burst pool; wants clear SLA for QPS floor during settlement windows.
poC_plan: 2-week POC: Week 1 synthetic replay at scaled QPS + profiling (kernel choice, batch sizes). Week 2 run with sampled production traces and validate autoscaler and burst pool. Deliverables: latency/QPS report, recommended GPU counts by model variant, suggested fallback policies and cost estimate.
decision_criteria: 1) measurable 95th pct latency under declared peak; 2) contractual throughput guarantees for settlement windows; 3) data residency and audit controls; 4) predictable cost model for reserved + burst capacity.
